sections.h2: What is different about selling a house in Lansing?
sections.html:
As Michigan's capital, Lansing straddles three counties. Most parcels are in Ingham, some are in Eaton to the west, and some in Clinton to the north. That decides where your deed is recorded, so look at your tax bill first.

The July 2025 estimate is 113,884 residents, 1.1 percent more than the 2020 base. Homes here sell at a lower price level than most of suburban Michigan, and only a little over half are owner-occupied, so a good share of sellers are landlords.

The city is usually described in four sections, and buyers use the same names:

  • Eastside, east of the Grand River, centered on Michigan Avenue and the Frandor shopping center
  • Westside, around the river's curve, the most mixed by income and home type
  • Northwestside, the smallest section, near the Capital Region International Airport
  • Southside, the fourth section

Old Town, with buildings from the mid-1800s, and REO Town, along Washington Avenue, are the two historic districts people mention first. A listing that names its section and nearest corridor is easier for buyers to place.

Government, education, insurance and health care keep Lansing's job base broad, and state and university work means steady renters and first-time buyers. Investors also look for small, older houses. If your house is a rental, expect investor interest first. If it is owner-occupied and updated, the broader market may pay more.

Lansing School District covers most of the city, yet pieces fall into Holt, East Lansing, Okemos, Mason, Waverly, Grand Ledge and DeWitt, so confirm the district by address before you describe the school zone.

Lansing is crossed by I-96, I-69, I-496, US-127, M-43 along Saginaw Street and Grand River Avenue, and M-99 on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard. Drivers reach Detroit or Grand Rapids in one highway run, which matters to buyers who commute or work for the state. A house within walking distance of a bus line or the river trail is worth naming in the listing text.

For 2020 to 2024, the numbers an appraiser or investor will start from are these:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $128,700
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 53.8%
  • Median gross rent: $993
  • Households: 51,588, with 2.17 persons per household
  • Median household income: $54,382

At that price level, one big repair bill takes a large bite out of a sale. Get two contractor quotes on any major item before you decide between listing and selling as-is.

Winters are cold, and snow averages 51.1 inches a season. For an older Lansing house, that points to the usual trouble spots: aging boilers and furnaces, thin attic insulation, frost-damaged porches and wet basements. Buyers pay attention to these items in any inspection report, so a clear service record helps in either a listing or a cash negotiation.

sections.h2: Do Lansing landlords have to register rentals before selling?
sections.html:
Yes. Lansing requires every rental property to be registered with Code Compliance, with the exception of an owner-occupied single-family dwelling. The fee schedule effective July 1, 2024 lists a $235 new registration fee, a $55 per building fee for a change of owner, and a base inspection fee of $175 per building for one and two family structures.

When a rental is sold, the buyer takes on the registration, the inspection history and any open citations. Late fees and failure-to-register fees are on the same schedule, so an unregistered rental costs more to sell than a registered one. Ask Code Compliance for the current forms before you list a rental.

Vacant houses face a separate risk. The schedule includes administrative fees for red-tagged properties, emergency board-up and demolition, all of which can be assessed against the parcel.

Lansing runs the same assessment cycle every year. These are the dates an owner should know:

Lansing yearly assessment cycle
DateWhat happens
February 14Last day to pay the prior year's winter taxes
Late FebruaryAssessment notices mailed
Second week of MarchMarch Board of Review hearings on valuation
June 1Deadline for a summer principal residence exemption
July 31Residential Michigan Tax Tribunal filing deadline
November 1Deadline for a winter principal residence exemption
December 31Tax day for the following year

Ask the Lansing Treasurer when unpaid bills move to the county, because that date decides who you pay at closing.

Your deed goes to whichever of the three county recorders holds the parcel. The state tax on it is $3.75 per $500 of price, a county tax is added on top, and a handful of family transfers escape both. The title company can tell you which line applies.

Within 45 days of closing the buyer reports the sale to Lansing's assessor, and the house's taxable value is rebased for the following year. You have 90 days after moving out to cancel your homestead school-tax exemption.

Weighing an investor's cash offer against a listing comes down to the net figure after taxes, recording costs and any city fees. Before you decide, collect these papers:

  • Your deed and the county named on your tax bill
  • Rental registration and inspection records, if the house was rented
  • Receipts for major repairs
  • A payoff figure from the Treasurer for any open tax bill

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, including open citations and a rental registration, which can save you the cost of repairs and a long wait for a lender.

sections.h2: Step by step: from offer to keys
sections.html:
A typical Lansing sale moves in a clear order. First, confirm the county on your tax bill, because that county's register of deeds will record the deed. Second, if the house is a rental, call Code Compliance and ask for the current forms and any open citations. Third, pick your route: a listing, a private sale or a cash offer. Fourth, ask the Treasurer for the status of both tax bills so nothing is left unpaid when the title company prorates them. Fifth, at closing, sign the deed and settlement statement and make sure the transfer tax lines match what the title company quoted.

After closing, mark your calendar for the 90-day window to cancel your homestead exemption. The buyer handles the assessor report, but it is smart to confirm with the title company that it was sent. A cash purchase skips the buyer's appraisal and loan approval, and it often skips the repair requests that follow a buyer's inspection. That can matter for an older house where the furnace, porch or basement would otherwise be negotiated line by line, and it gives you a firm closing date to plan your move around.

faqs.q: Which county records a deed for a Lansing house?
faqs.a: The county where the parcel sits records it. Lansing spans Ingham, Eaton and Clinton counties, so read the county on your tax bill and ask that county's register of deeds.

faqs.q: How much is the Lansing rental registration fee?
faqs.a: A new registration costs $235 and a change of owner costs $55 per building under the schedule effective July 1, 2024. Inspections start at a $175 base fee for one and two family buildings.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Lansing?
faqs.a: The median value for 2020 to 2024 is $128,700, with median gross rent at $993.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Lansing winter taxes?
faqs.a: February 14 is the last day to pay winter taxes. Ask the Lansing Treasurer when open bills move to the county.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell the city I sold my house?
faqs.a: The buyer reports the sale to the assessor, and you cancel your homestead exemption within 90 days of moving out.
